name: Durvalumab

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1κ anti-PD-L1 antibody with a triple Fc mutation that reduces effector function.

tagline: PD-L1 inhibitor that set the standard after chemoradiation in stage III lung cancer
summary: Durvalumab is a human monoclonal antibody against PD-L1. Its PACIFIC trial established consolidation immunotherapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer, and it is also used in small cell lung cancer, biliary tract cancer, liver cancer and endometrial cancer.
mechanism: Durvalumab binds PD-L1 and blocks its interaction with PD-1 and CD80, restoring the activity of T cells suppressed within the tumour microenvironment.
Its engineered Fc does not mediate antibody-dependent cytotoxicity or complement activation. It is sometimes combined with tremelimumab, an anti-CTLA-4 antibody.
uses: Unresectable stage III NSCLC after chemoradiotherapy
Small cell lung cancer (extensive-stage with chemotherapy; limited-stage after chemoradiation)

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA approves Imfinzi in May for previously treated urothelial carcinoma (indication later withdrawn in 2021).

history.title: PACIFIC approval
history.detail: Approved for stage III NSCLC after chemoradiotherapy, having improved progression-free and overall survival.

history.title: Biliary and liver cancer
history.detail: Approved for biliary tract cancer (TOPAZ-1) and, with tremelimumab, for HCC (HIMALAYA).

history.title: Limited-stage SCLC
history.detail: Approved after chemoradiotherapy for limited-stage SCLC (ADRIATIC).

history.title: Bladder cancer
history.detail: Approved perioperatively with chemotherapy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NIAGARA).

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

serious: Immune-mediated endocrinopathies (thyroiditis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency, type 1 diabetes)

facts: PACIFIC was the first trial to show a survival benefit for immunotherapy after chemoradiotherapy in stage III NSCLC.
Durvalumab with tremelimumab (STRIDE regimen) uses a single priming dose of the anti-CTLA-4 antibody.
